temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Thin, about ½ inch (1 cm) 400°F / 205°C · 8 min 425°F / 220°C · 10 min Standard, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) 400°F / 205°C · 12 min 425°F / 220°C · 15 min Thick, about 1½ inches (4 cm) 400°F / 205°C · 16 min 425°F / 220°C · 20 min Why pork chops turn dry and chalky Modern pork is lean. With little fat running through the meat, a chop has nothing to protect it once it goes past done, and it turns dry, tight and chalky within a few minutes. The habit of cooking pork until it is grey all the way through comes from old guidance; today a chop is safe at 145°F with a short rest, when the centre is still faintly pink and juicy. Thin chops are the hardest to get right in an air fryer because they overcook before the outside browns. Buy chops at least an inch thick if you can, and if you only have thin ones, cook them at the top of the time range and check early. Worked example Two 1-inch boneless chops, brined for an hour, dried and rubbed with oil and spices. Preheat for 4 minutes, cook at 400°F and flip at 6 minutes; they should reach 145°F at around 12 minutes. Thin ½-inch chops need about 8 minutes, thick 1½-inch ones about 16. In a conventional oven the same chops take 425°F for around 15 minutes. How to tell they are done Measure from the side into the thickest part, away from any bone. 145°F (63°C) followed by a three-minute rest is the safe target; the centre will be a pale blush and the juices clear. Bone-in chops cook a little slower near the bone, so check there last. If you cut into a chop, the meat should be moist and just opaque, not grey and fibrous. Before they go in A simple brine of a tablespoon of salt to two cups of water for 30–60 minutes makes the biggest difference to juiciness. Dry the chops well afterwards. Snip through the fat around the edge in two or three places so the chop does not curl as it cooks. A spice rub with a little sugar browns nicely but watch it in the last minutes. Related presets Bacon 350°F · 9 min Steak 400°F · 10 min · flip at 5 Sausages 370°F · 12 min · flip at 6 425°F oven to air fryer, every food → Oven to air fryer converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How long do pork chops take in the air fryer? About 12 minutes at 400°F for 1-inch chops, flipped at 6 minutes. Thin chops take around 8 minutes and thick ones around 16. What temperature should pork chops reach? 145°F (63°C), then rest for three minutes. A faint pink centre at that temperature is safe and much juicier. Should I brine pork chops for the air fryer? If you have 30 minutes, yes. Lean chops gain a lot of moisture from a short brine, and it makes them more forgiving if they cook a minute too long. Bone-in or boneless pork chops in the air fryer? Both work at the same temperature. Bone-in chops take a minute or two longer and stay slightly juicier near the bone. What is the oven equivalent for pork chops? 425°F for around 15 minutes in a conventional oven, or 400°F for 13 minutes in a fan oven.
